summary: The cap-threshold and bathtub-equality argument correctly proves a unique support contact, and equality of cap indicators together with interior-cutting hyperplanes correctly forces every nonzero normal at that contact onto the same positive ray. Under the accepted predecessor identities, zero interaction forces every pairwise gap at a loaded endpoint to vanish, hence collapses the endpoint contacts and normalized directions; the load, balance, component-ray, and component-barycenter conclusions then follow by the stated exact identities and correct double-counting. Boundary cases, including dimension one and degree-one loaded endpoints, are handled without a gap.
